sections.html:
Canyon County's Nampa counted an estimated 120,384 people as of July 1, 2025, a 19.9 percent jump over the 100,414 base from April 2020. Its nickname is Heart of the Treasure Valley, and Interstate 84 passes through roughly 33.5 square miles of city.

Owners outnumber renters. Between 2020 and 2024, 70.2 percent of homes were owner-occupied, with a median value of $370,800 and median gross rent of $1,420. Use that median loosely: one house can be priced far from it in either direction.

Growth shows up as new subdivisions on the edges while older houses cluster near the center. Each group draws its own buyers and its own repair list.

sections.h2: Railroad roots and the street grid
sections.html: Nampa started when the Oregon Short Line Railroad laid track through the site in the early 1880s, bound from Granger, Wyoming, to Huntington, Oregon. Downtown streets are skewed because they follow the tracks, which run northwest to southeast. Union Pacific still operates on that line.

Hot dry summers and cold winters with little rain define the weather. Sun and heat wear a house down most, plus an occasional hard freeze. Only about 11.4 inches of precipitation falls in a year, mostly in December and January at roughly 1.4 inches each.

The average July high is near 91 degrees, with 109 as the record. An average January night is about 21 degrees, and minus 26 is the coldest on record.

  • Air conditioners work hard, so buyers check how old yours is.
  • Strong sun ages roofing, fences and exterior paint sooner.
  • Lake Ethel began as an irrigation reservoir, so some buyers ask whether a lot has irrigation service.

Nampa, Skyview, Columbia and Union high schools belong to the Nampa School District, which serves most of town. Another part is in Vallivue, where Ridgevue High School is located, and a few blocks are in West Ada. Buyers focused on one school need the district boundary, not the mailing address.

Two colleges, the College of Western Idaho and Northwest Nazarene University, are based here. Four I-84 exits serve Nampa, Idaho 55 and Idaho 45 cut across it, and ValleyRide operates local buses.

Selling needs no permit. Still, unpermitted work tends to surface once a buyer or title company digs in. The city requires a residential building permit for a new home, addition or remodel, and the Building Department handles questions at 208-468-5435.

Property complaints go to the Code Compliance and Community Relations Division. A neglected vacant home can be reported at 208-468-5473 or through an online complaint.

  • Mow and tidy an empty house, because neglected vacant homes attract complaints.
  • Did your own repairs? Learn whether a permit was pulled, and admit it to the buyer if you cannot tell.
  • Keep every code notice, as buyers ask for them.

Canyon County values and bills Nampa property by calendar year, with a January 1 lien date. The value on that day is what gets taxed.

DateWhat happens in Canyon County
JuneAssessment notices are mailed
Fourth Monday in JuneDeadline to appeal the assessed value
Second Monday in JulyCommissioners finish as the Board of Equalization
Fourth Monday in NovemberTax notices must be sent
December 20First half or full payment due
June 20Second half due

Your case is that the property was worth less than assessed on January 1. Get the appeal form from the Assessor's office and file it in writing by the fourth Monday in June. The Board of Equalization weighs whether the value is fair and accurate. Your ability to pay is not part of the review.

Unhappy with the board's ruling? You can go on to the State Board of Tax Appeals and then District Court. Canyon County's Data Hub displays five years of assessment and tax history, useful for building your argument. The county's assessment page walks through the steps.

Manufactured housing has a harsher rule. Miss the December 20 first half and that half turns delinquent, making the entire tax due at once. The treasurer's office, at (208) 454-7354, can answer questions.

With any house that owes tax, the title company locates the balance and settles it from sale proceeds at closing. Mention it to the buyer at the start so nothing comes as a shock.

Idaho Code section 55-2501 and the sections after it require a property condition disclosure form from sellers of residences with up to four units. It is your chance to lay out the material physical problems the house has.

Specifics matter. Say if the furnace quits in cold snaps, one corner of the roof leaks, or an earlier owner built an addition with no permit. Idaho Code 55-2508 supplies the standard wording.

sections.h2: What to gather before you sell
sections.html:
A short folder of paperwork speeds everything up. Collect these before you ask anyone for an offer:

  • Your most recent Canyon County tax notice and, if you filed one, your appeal paperwork.
  • Permit records for any addition or remodel, or a note saying you are unsure whether one exists.
  • Any letter from Code Compliance, along with proof of what you did in response.
  • Your draft of the disclosure form, with every known problem written out.
  • Payoff information for any mortgage on the house.

At closing, the title company checks ownership, confirms what is owed on the property and pays those balances first. What remains is yours, and you walk away without having made repairs or hosted showings. Because a cash sale has no lender appraisal or loan underwriting, the date is mostly set by how quickly the title work clears.

Houses in good condition may net more through a listing. Cash trades part of that price for speed and certainty. Let the house's needs and your closing deadline settle it.

  • Choose a listing for a move-in ready house when showings are no trouble.
  • Choose cash when repairs outrun your budget, you inherited the property, or payments are slipping.

Because we buy as-is, there is no cleaning, fixing or staging. Our offer follows once we know the details, and refusing it is free. Prices are never quoted ahead of time.

The sequence is simple. Send the address and condition details, receive an offer, and if you accept, a title company manages closing and clears any mortgage or tax debt from your proceeds. Bring your latest tax bill and any code notices to the first conversation, because they sharpen the offer. Also say whether the house is occupied or empty, and whether you have a deadline. Both change how a buyer plans the purchase.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a Nampa house?
faqs.a: December 20 is the due date, and half may be paid then with the rest on June 20. Notices must be mailed by the fourth Monday in November.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal my Canyon County assessment?
faqs.a: It falls on the fourth Monday in June, shortly after June's assessment notices. Request the written form from the Assessor's office.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Nampa house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes, open code issues are fine for an as-is purchase. Share any Code Compliance notices so our offer accounts for them.

faqs.q: Which Nampa school district is my house in?
faqs.a: The Nampa School District covers most of the city, Vallivue covers parts, and a few blocks sit in West Ada. Look up your address on the district map before listing.
Quickly. The 2025 estimate of 120,384 is up 19.9 percent from 100,414 in April 2020.
